claims: Gary Woodland won the Houston Open on March 29, 2026.
The Houston Open win was Gary Woodland's first PGA Tour win since the 2019 U.S. Open.
The Houston Open win was Gary Woodland's first PGA Tour win since undergoing surgery to remove a benign brain tumor.
Gary Woodland secured his fifth PGA Tour win at the Houston Open in March 2026.
In May 2023, an MRI revealed a lesion on Gary Woodland's brain.
The lesion on Gary Woodland's brain was causing severe symptoms including fear, anxiety, and partial seizures.
On September 18, 2023, Gary Woodland underwent a craniotomy to remove the tumor.
Doctors removed the majority of Gary Woodland's tumor.
Gary Woodland's tumor was determined to be benign.
A small portion of Gary Woodland's tumor remains.
The small portion of Gary Woodland's tumor remains because it was too close to critical areas near the amygdala and the optic tract to safely remove.
The area near the amygdala affects fear and anxiety.
In January 2024, Gary Woodland returned to competitive golf at the Sony Open.
In early 2026, Gary Woodland revealed he had been diagnosed with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) about a year prior.
Gary Woodland's PTSD diagnosis led to significant mental and emotional struggles after the operation.
Gary Woodland described experiencing intense fear, anxiety, and hypervigilance on the golf course, particularly when people were behind him.
Gary Woodland said his public disclosure of his PTSD battle lifted a massive weight off his shoulders.
In 2025, a diagnosis revealed the need to manage Gary Woodland's remaining tumor.
Gary Woodland was honored with the PGA Tour Courage Award in February 2025.
